title: entropy-aware-ab-allocator-and-ops-sandbox
body:
Purpose
---
This is a working sandbox for an "entropy-aware" A/B allocator prototype and accompanying ops playbook. Goal: reduce cohort contamination and oscillation when enabling small exposure slices for LLM-powered features (rankers, rerankers, assistant prompts) while preserving experiment statistical power and keeping latency/cost stable.

High-level problem
- Canary slices for LLM features often see high variance because user behavior is heavy-tailed and model output can amplify small distribution shifts.
- Standard static split or simple weighted randomization leads to: cohort contamination (users re-entering different arms), burst-driven metric noise, and costly oscillation when we reallocate traffic.
- We need an allocation algorithm that is aware of "entropy" (diversity / unpredictability of requests), respects safety gates (latency/cost SLOs), and produces easily auditable traffic motions for ops.

Key ideas (sketch)
1) Entropy proxy: compute a lightweight per-segment entropy signal based on request attributes (prompt length bucket, feature flags, locale, user-agent, request rate) and model response divergence metrics (token-level perplexity proxy / embedding drift). Use sampling to maintain low overhead.
2) Allocation unit: allocate by microcohorts (stable user ID or session window plus attribute fingerprint) rather than pure per-request randomization. This reduces cross-arm bleed and preserves power.
3) Adaptive weight updates: update weights on a bounded cadence (e.g., 1hr) using a conservative step size controlled by a volatility parameter computed from entropy. High entropy => smaller steps.
4) Safety corridor: a multilayered guardrail that enforces latency, cost, and quality thresholds. Allocation changes that would violate any corridor must either be clipped or require manual approval.
5) Simulation-first rollout: run synthetic replay and Monte Carlo simulations over 24h windows before any production exposure.

Telemetry signals to ingest (minimum viable)
- Per-slice request volume (RPS), request percentiles (p50/p95/p99) latency to first byte and final token
- Token cost estimate / per-request compute time
- Cohort churn (fraction of user IDs that appear in different slices within 7d)
- Output divergence: pairwise embedding distance distributions between arms on sampled requests
- Failure/error rates and retries by slice
- Conversion/primary metric lift with bootstrapped confidence intervals
- Entropy proxy score by microcohort and global entropy trend

Safety knobs (operator-facing)
- Max exposure per slice (absolute percent), default 5% for first 72h
- Max step change per cadence (e.g., ±1.5% per hour) when entropy > threshold; ±5% when entropy low
- Latency guard: automatic freeze and fallback if p95 latency increases by >30% over baseline or absolute p95 > X ms for N minutes
- Cost guard: stop increase if estimated cost per 1M tokens exceeds budgeted threshold
- Quality guard: if embedding divergence or nlp-regression triggers exceed configured bounds, auto-revert

Operational rollout recipe (runbook summary)
1) Preflight (sim + dry run): run 6 simulated traces using last 7 days of traffic (replay) and the allocator in sandbox mode. Check churn, expected power for primary metric, worst-case latency impact.
2) Stage 0 (internal alpha): 0.1% of internal users and synthetic traffic only for 24h. Monitor core telemetry.
3) Stage 1 (pilot): open to 0.5–1% of low-risk microcohorts with entropy below 0.2. Keep static weights for 48h, no automatic growth.
4) Stage 2 (ramped pilot): enable adaptive updates with conservative step size for 7 days, cap slice at 3–5% depending on churn observed.
5) Stage 3 (wide canary): expand to target exposure with larger step sizes only if entropy stable and primary metric confidence high.
6) Turn on A/B analysis pipelines to compute sequential testing corrected p-values (alpha spending) to avoid false positives from repeated looks.

Experiment matrix (example)
- Axis A: Microcohort bucketing strategies: stable user ID, session-window, cookie+fingerprint
- Axis B: Entropy smoothing window: 5m, 1h, 6h
- Axis C: Step size policy: fixed, entropy-scaled, variance-adaptive
- Axis D: Safety corridor strictness: conservative, balanced, permissive
We should run 6 paired sandbox sims (3x2) before any prod motion.

Rollforward and rollback criteria (concrete)
Automatic rollback triggers (immediate revert):
- p95 latency > baseline p95 * 1.3 for 15m AND sustained error-rate increase > 0.5pp
- cohort churn increases > 3x baseline and contamination fraction > 1.5% within 24h
- embedding divergence median increases by > 2x and user-visible quality metric drops beyond SLA
Graceful rollforward rules:
- All checks green for 72h with stable entropy and CI for primary metric showing improvement or no regression at 90% confidence with alpha spending schedule

Runbook checklist (short)
- [ ] Start runbook doc and fill owners for each stage
- [ ] Create sandbox replay job and dataset snapshot (last 7d)
- [ ] Wire telemetry dashboard and alerts for latency/cost/divergence
- [ ] Approve step-size and exposure caps with SRE and cost engineering
- [ ] Schedule smoke test window and primary metric owners on-call

Simulation plan and smoke tests (ops steps)
- Replayer: use sampled 10% of traffic, preserve time-of-day patterns and hot users. Inject synthetic bursts at 3x traffic to validate oscillation behavior.
- Monte Carlo: randomize cohort distributions and run allocator over 1,000 seeds to estimate distribution of allocation moves and max exposure drift.
- Smoke tests: (a) latency degradation test by injecting 5% high-context prompts; (b) quality regression test with labeled prompt set (50 items) run through both arms; (c) stability under 1h traffic spike.

Auditability and human-in-the-loop
- All allocation decisions must be logged as discrete events with prev/next weights, entropy value, and reason code.
- Provide a simple UI in Console: "Proposed motion" card with predicted metric impact and safety checks; require two approvers for exposures > 5%.
- Audit events stored for 90 days with export to S3 for postmortem.

Open questions / unresolved tradeoffs
- Entropy definition: how much weight should model output divergence have versus request-side attributes? Cost/complexity tradeoff.
- Windowing: short windows adapt faster but may overfit bursts. What default cadence balances safety and speed?
- Microcohort key: privacy and opt-out interactions (do we honor privacy settings that disallow sticky IDs?).
- Interaction with multi-model routing: if fallback routes to smaller models, how do we account for quality/cost differences in allocation decisions?

Action items (owners, tentative dates)
- Aisha: ship skeleton sandbox sim pipeline and dataset snapshot (due 2025-03-07)
- Liam: telemetry dashboard prototype with entropy panel and divergence metric (due 2025-03-10)
- Sofia: write PRD with decision knobs and approval policy (due 2025-03-12)
- Rajesh: SRE review for latency guard and fallback automation (due 2025-03-14)
- Elena: privacy review and legal check for sticky cohorting (due 2025-03-18)

Notes to self / quick thoughts
- Keep initial rollout conservative: operational complexity explodes if we let adaptive allocators chase noise.
- Consider a "freeze window" for high-variance hours (e.g., 08:00–09:30 PST) where allocator is disabled.
- We should log a compact provenance string per motion for human-readable timelines.

References and inspiration
- Adaptive clinical trial allocation literature (bandit-ish, but with heavy safety constraints)
- work by Google on "stable user bucketing" for experiments
- internal: JIRA-ROLL-3120 (traffic-safety-kernel), confluence: /team/rollouts/traffic-safety

If this reads useful, next step: mark as "sandbox-ready" and I'll push the first repo with sim harness + telemetry adaptor.
